text:
alex (AcmeApp): Hey team — running into a hard failure when customers try to sign in with Google OAuth. They hit our /auth/google/callback and immediately get redirected back to /login with an error banner: "Login failed: state mismatch". Happening for ~10% of users, mostly on Chrome. No code param in query on some requests.

maria (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, alex. Can you paste the exact redirect URI configured in your Google Console and the callback URL you're using in the app? Also, any recent changes to cookies or SameSite? :thinking_face:

alex (AcmeApp): Google Console redirect URI is https://app.acme.co/auth/google/callback (no trailing slash). Our client initiates auth from https://app.acme.co/login via a popup. We use PKCE (S256) and store code_verifier/state in a cookie named __acme_oauth. Cookie flags: Secure; SameSite=Lax; HttpOnly. We just moved to a new domain mapping (app.acme.co -> app.app-hosted.net proxy) last week.

ben (AuthEng): Hmm proxy change could explain it. When using popup + cross-site redirect, SameSite=Lax will block cookies on cross-site POST/GET in some flows. If Google redirects through an intermediate domain or the proxy changes host header, the cookie may not be sent back, causing missing state/code_verifier. Two quick checks: (1) capture the full callback URL users hit (including query string) and (2) confirm whether the browser actually included __acme_oauth on that request.

alex (AcmeApp): Repro steps I ran locally: open https://app.acme.co/login -> click Sign in with Google -> popup opens to accounts.google.com -> after auth, popup closes and parent navigates to /auth/google/callback?code=4/0AX4...&scope=email&state=abc123. But on failing runs I see /auth/google/callback with only error=access_denied and no state param or sometimes state= (empty). Server logs show: "callback handler: state mismatch (expected 'abc123' got '')". Attached a screenshot of devtools network for one failing request.

maria (Support): @ben any ideas on whether SameSite=Lax could drop the cookie for popup redirects?

ben (AuthEng): Yes — Lax allows top-level GET navigations but blocks cookies on some cross-site contexts, especially when the flow involves a POST or if Google decides to do a cross-site redirect through an accounts subdomain. Also noteworthy: some browser extensions and cross-site trackers modify behavior. Recommended changes: set SameSite=None; Secure on __acme_oauth (and ensure not HttpOnly if client JS needs to read verifier), or store state/code_verifier in sessionStorage before opening popup and read from parent after popup returns.

alex (AcmeApp): We currently set HttpOnly because we thought it was safer. The app JS never reads the cookie — server performs exchange. Would making it SameSite=None + Secure and keep HttpOnly work? I'm worried about CSRF surface.

ben (AuthEng): If server needs the cookie, keep HttpOnly. SameSite=None + Secure will allow cross-site delivery from Google redirect. That should fix cookies missing on callback. CSRF should still be mitigated by state value itself. Alternative is storing state in a signed server side session keyed by a short session cookie (also SameSite=None). Both OK.

alex (AcmeApp): One more oddity: I saw one failing URL where the redirect_uri parameter included a trailing slash (https://app.acme.co/auth/google/callback/) but our registered redirect uri has no trailing slash. Could that cause Google to reject/strip parameters?

maria (Support): Good catch. Redirect URI must exactly match what's in the console (including trailing slash). If they vary, Google may consider it invalid and behave unpredictably. Check server logs for rejected_client or invalid_redirect_uri errors from Google.

alex (AcmeApp): Logs show occasional 400 from accounts.google.com with body: {"error":"invalid_request","error_description":"Invalid redirect_uri"}. On others we get 200 but no state. So two issues likely: redirect_uri mismatch and cookie not sent.

ben (AuthEng): Agreed. Action plan: (1) Update Google Console to include both variants (with/without trailing slash) OR normalize outgoing redirect_uri to exact registered value. (2) Change cookie: SameSite=None; Secure (and keep HttpOnly if server-only). (3) If using proxy, ensure Host header and TLS are preserved so Google returns to same registered origin. (4) Add extra logging to capture full querystring on callback for failed requests and browser User-Agent.

alex (AcmeApp): I'll try updating cookie flags and normalizing redirect_uri. Quick Q: how to debug PKCE code_verifier mismatch? We generate code_verifier and keep only in cookie; if cookie missing, server can't compute expected code_verifier and fails with mismatch. Any debug hooks we can add?

ben (AuthEng): Add a temporary debug header when initiating auth (only visible in your dev logs) that stores the expected state hash keyed by transaction id, or log a truncated code_challenge and lookup on callback. But be careful with PII/security — mask values. Example in server logs: "init oauth tx=tx123 code_challenge=E3b..." then on callback: "callback tx=tx123 code=... state=... cookie_sent=true/false".

alex (AcmeApp): Got it. I'll roll a change to set SameSite=None and add extra logs. One more ask: some customers reported 'redirect loop' where they repeatedly get bounced between /auth/google/start and /auth/google/callback. Any pointers?

ben (AuthEng): Redirect loops often occur when the app tries to retry auth on missing state but doesn't clear the old cookies/params, or when callback handler fails and redirects back to start without clearing session. Ensure that on callback failure you show an error (don't auto-retry) and clear any partial oauth cookies. Also check for double redirects from proxy rewriting the path.

maria (Support): I'll follow up with a short checklist for you, alex, and mark this thread as escalated to AuthEng. If you can paste one raw failing callback request (headers + full URL) once you have it, we'll confirm the fix. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Deploy of auth-fixes branch to staging succeeded (build #2048) :white_check_mark:

alex (AcmeApp): Thanks @maria @ben — I'll test on staging and post the failing request if it still occurs. Appreciate the quick triage.

deploy-bot: Noted escalation to AuthEng queue.

maria (Support): Closing loop — ping us when you have logs and we'll re-open. Good luck! :rocket:
